exercise.name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press
library_steps: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells at your chest, palms facing each other.
Press them up until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
exercise.one_line_summary: Flat bench, palms facing each other, elbows tucked about 40 deg from the body at the bottom with forearms vertical; press to near-straight arms over the lower chest. Chest is the target; triceps and front delts help.

setup.target: Lie flat: head, upper back and hips on the pad, feet flat on the floor either side of the bench, knees about 90-110 deg.
setup.why: Both EMG studies kept head and thoracic back on the bench.

setup.target: Neutral grip: palms face each other, handles run head-to-foot, thumbs toward the head.
setup.tolerance: handle within 15 deg of the body's long axis
setup.why: Defines the exercise; Muyor 2023 tested a neutral grip against a prone grip.

movement.measure: upper arm angle from the torso side line, 0 = by the side
0 = out to the side, +90 = straight up out of the chest, negative = below the torso line
movement.start: -25 deg (elbows a little below the bench line)
flat on the bench, feet on floor

muscles.emg: Seated neutral-grip press: clavicular ~30% MVIC, more than the wide prone bench press (~25%) (S1). Flat bench gives the highest sternal/costal activity of five angles (S2).
~12-16% MVIC in bench press variants, higher with the narrower grip (S1); ~15% at all bench angles (S2).
~24% MVIC, no grip or exercise difference (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms straight out from the shoulders at the bottom, palms drifting to face the feet.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Turns it into a regular wide press; the library cue is elbows close to the sides.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Bridge under the lower back at the top.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Both studies kept the back and head on the bench.

sources.citation: Muyor JM, Rodriguez-Ridao D, Oliva-Lozano JM. 2023. Comparison of muscle activity between the horizontal bench press and the seated chest press exercises using several grips. J Hum Kinet 87:23-34.
sources.what_it_gave: n=20, 60% 1RM, 2 s/2 s. Neutral grip seated press: clavicular pec ~30% MVIC vs ~25% wide bench; front delt ~24% everywhere; triceps 16% narrow vs 12% wide bench.

sources.citation: Rodriguez-Ridao D, Antequera-Vique JA, Martin-Fuentes I, Muyor JM. 2020. Effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid, and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339.
sources.what_it_gave: 0-60 deg benches. Flat bench highest sternal/costal pec. Technique: lowered to ~1 cm over the sternum, shoulders ~45 deg abducted, pressed to straight arms without hyperextension, head and back on the bench.

clip_check.check: End: arms near straight, dumbbells over lower-mid chest
Hands on the handles, palms facing each other
Chest is the strongest red in both pictures
